about:
# Reforged UI for WoW: Forever

A World of Warcraft: Forever addon that replaces the bottom of the screen with
the Warcraft III console, with a theme for every playable race: Human, Dwarf,
Gnome, Night Elf, Orc, Tauren, Troll, Undead (Forsaken or Scourge) and
Skyborne (High Order and Windshapers).

The console is a port of a WoW 1.12 console addon: its layout, art, fonts and options menu,
rebuilt for the current engine (Edit Mode, secret values, protected frames).
All console art and the font in `ReforgedUI/art` are the original addon's. Reforged UI
adds the top bar with the day/night clock and data broker feeds.

![16:9 Orc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexHaible/WoW-UI-Addon/master/docs/previews/16x9-orc.png)

## What it does

Left to right, as in the original addon with its "Center UI" option, which is always on:
the console sits in the middle of the screen with the original addon's chat width (on a
16:9 screen it fills the width, on 21:9 and 32:9 screens the rest of the
screen stays free on either side).

- **Minimap block**: a square minimap with mouse-wheel zoom, the zone name on
  its bottom or top edge, the tracking button in the round slot below it, the
  mail slot (a grey letter when there is no mail) and three action slots
  beside it. Other addons' minimap buttons go in a compartment: click the bag
  just above the map's top-right corner to open or close a flyout of them
  (Blizzard's own buttons line up along the top edge of the map); the minimap's day/night indicator is hidden (the top bar has the
  clock). Our calendar button leads that row in place of Blizzard's: today's
  date on a note, with a pulsing letter while calendar invitations wait;
  click it for the calendar, hover it for the week's events.
- **Portrait block**: animated 3D portrait (click to target yourself,
  right-click for your menu), health and power bars under it, rest/combat,
  group leader and PvP icons. The background pulses red under the low health
  threshold.
- **Incoming heals**: every health bar (player, target in either mode,
  the target bar, target of target, pet) shows the game's heal prediction
  after the health fill, your own heals bright teal and others' darker
  (HealPrediction.lua).
- **Hero screen**: name, level and class, the experience bar with rested
  experience (hover for the numbers, right-click for its colour: purple,
  blue or none), a thin reputation strip under it for the faction ticked
  "Show as Experience Bar" (in its standing's colour; hover for the numbers,
  click for the reputation panel; "Reputation bar" in the options or
  `/rui repbar off` turns it off) and four stat icons. Each shows main hand, off hand (block
  chance and value with a shield), ranged, ammo (yellow under 400, red under
  200), attack power (ranged for hunters), spell power, healing, armour
  (the default for the fourth), dodge chance, parry chance, resistances
  (fire, nature, frost, shadow and arcane as coloured numbers),
  strength, agility, intellect (with Warcraft III's hero attribute art),
  stamina, spirit, crit chance (the best of melee, ranged and spell, with
  the Blademaster's Critical Strike icon) or nothing (an empty socket),
  chosen per class from each icon's right-click menu
  or the options' Hero screen page. Druid forms and Ghost Wolf swap
  the icons like the original addon.
- **Target**: by default the hero screen switches to your target, as
  selecting a unit in Warcraft III: its portrait, name (coloured by reaction
  or class), level and classification, health and power bars with numbers,
  your combo points and its cast bar. Your own bars under the portrait stay
  yours; clearing the target brings your hero back. "Wall plate" in the
  options (or `/rui target plate`) instead puts the target in a small
  portrait arch standing on the wall above the stats panel. Either way the
  target's target is a small unit icon above the portrait (blue when it is
  you, else green, yellow or red), with the target's buffs and debuffs
  beside it (above the plate in plate mode). Those are Blizzard's own aura
  icons: in combat the game lets no addon read a target's auras, so
  Blizzard's target frame stays with everything but its auras made
  invisible, and the "Reforged UI" Edit Mode layout places it (buffs on
  top) so the icons land there. "Target aura size" in the options (or
  `/rui aurasize 100-200`) makes them bigger through that layout's Frame
  Size for the target frame, as far as a full row still fits on the wall.
  The wall plate can be moved: hold Shift and drag it out of combat, or
  drag it while Edit Mode is open (it shows then, target or not). Its
  cast bar, combo points and tag are on it, the target of target follows
  to stand beside it, and the buff and debuff icons follow above it through
  the Edit Mode layout (after a reload). Its place is kept from the
  screen's bottom centre, the same on every theme. "Wall plate size" (or
  `/rui plate size 50-150`) scales it, "Mirror wall plate" (or `/rui plate
  mirror on`) turns it round, and `/rui plate reset` puts it back.
  "Show target of target" (or `/rui tot off`) turns the target of target
  icon off where it gets in the way (out of combat; the target of target
  bar can stand in for it).
  Move the Target Frame in Edit Mode and the icons stay where you put them
  (the size option still applies); a target display switch or `/rui auras
  reset` puts them back in that display's place.
  The game puts a hostile target's debuffs on the bottom rows and its buffs
  above them; "Target buffs first" (or `/rui buffsfirst on`) puts the buffs
  on the bottom rows, on the portrait, and the debuffs after them, for every
  target. It does so by having Blizzard's aura container treat every target
  as friendly, so on hostile creatures it also shows other players'
  debuffs, as the game's "show all debuffs" option would.
  Your threat on the target (the tooltip's percentage, from
  UnitDetailedThreatSituation) stands at the top of its portrait and on the
  target bar's top edge while you are on its threat list, coloured by threat
  status; "Show threat on target" (or `/rui threat off`) turns it off. Where
  the game makes it secret (bosses, in instances) the client formats the
  number and it shows in white, only while you are in combat.
  Left-click targets, right-click opens the unit menu.
  The target's cast bar reads the game's cast info as it is: for any unit
  but you and your pet that info is secret, so it goes straight into the bar
  and is never compared or added up.
  For the target's health nearer the middle of the screen, the options'
  "Target bar" (or `/rui targetbar on`) adds a small free-standing bar with
  its name, level, health and power (and its cast bar underneath while it
  casts), in either mode. It is click-through
  until you hold Shift out of combat (or open Edit Mode), then drag it anywhere; its place
  is saved on its own and never touches the Edit Mode layout.
  "Target of target bar" (or `/rui totbar on`) is the same window for the
  target's target (no cast bar), moved and saved on its own; it starts to
  the right of the target bar. "Target bar size" (or `/rui barsize
  100-200`) makes both bigger, each kept in its place.
- **Action grid**: action bars 1-3, twelve slots each. These are Blizzard's
  own buttons, moved into the grid and reskinned, so bindings, paging,
  cooldowns and proc glows work as usual. The stance buttons (Paladin auras,
  Warrior stances, Druid forms, ...) stand in a row on the wall above the grid,
  as in Warcraft III; these are Blizzard's buttons too. Open Edit Mode to drag
  the row elsewhere by its blue outline (`/rui stance reset` puts it back), or
  tick "Leave stance buttons to my bar addon" in the options (`/rui stance
  off`, needs a reload) to let Blizzard's stance bar or your bar addon have
  them; with Dominos loaded that happens by itself. "Hide stance buttons"
  (`/rui stance hide`) makes them invisible and click-through instead; their
  key bindings still work. The pet bar starts in a
  row just above them (on their row, for classes without stances), at about
  their size, and is Blizzard's Edit Mode bar, so you can move and resize it
  in Edit Mode.
- **Inventory**: the bags in the 2x3 inventory (backpack top-left, bags 1-4,
  reagent bag bottom-right where the client has one) with the key ring to its
  right, under the chat buttons. Clicks go through Blizzard's own bag buttons, so bag addons such as
  BetterBags open as usual; drag a bag onto a slot to equip it.
- **Chat area**: the main chat window and its input box fill the black area
  at the right end of the console, which can be raised. The options
  cogwheel sits in its bottom-right corner.
- **End caps**: a pillar in the theme's style closes each end of the
  console, since it always stands in mid-screen. On 21:9 the chat area
  narrows a little where it needs to for both to fit; on 16:9 they are past
  the screen edges.
- **Top bar** (Reforged UI): the day/night clock in the middle (with a
  capsule under it showing the server or local time, 24 or 12 hour, or
  hidden, set in the options) with
  Blizzard's micro buttons either side of it (character, professions,
  talents, group finder, collections, ... in Blizzard's order, then Legacy
  and the game menu to close the row; no quest log, social or map buttons,
  which have their keys, and no adventure guide or shop), and slots for
  LibDataBroker feeds, the same distance either side of the centre and out
  to the screen edges: gold, bag space and durability fill the first three
  (right of the clock; hover the gold for every character's gold and a total
  per faction, Horde and Alliance apart). Our ping and FPS feed shows world
  latency on the left of its slot and the framerate on the right (hover it for
  home latency and bandwidth); a zone feed shows where you are, coloured by
  PvP status like the minimap's; a calendar feed shows what is on now (or the
  next event and when) and waiting invitations, with the week in its tooltip
  and the calendar a click away; a reputation feed shows the faction ticked
  "Show as Experience Bar" and its progress through the standing (right-click
  for its name, standing or what's left to the next standing; details and
  this session's gain in the tooltip, a click opens the reputation panel);
  a loot feed shows the group's loot method and, for Group Loot, Need before
  Greed and Master Looter, the loot threshold in its quality colour ("Solo"
  out of a group; the tooltip explains the method and names the master
  looter; the group leader right-clicks it to change method, master looter
  or threshold, Loot.lua). Right-click an empty
  slot (Alt-right-click a filled one) to choose any feed, or one of the
  game's own panels (character, spellbook, talents, skills, quest log,
  social, guild, world map, game menu, ...: whichever the client has),
  shown by name in the theme's menu font and colour. A panel's slot opens it with a secure click on Blizzard's micro button for
  it, so it opens untainted and in combat too. The micro buttons
  are Blizzard's own, moved and scaled to the bar, so their tooltips, alerts
  and disabled states work as usual; the micro menu itself stays empty and
  click-through wherever Edit Mode puts it. **Hide top bar** in the options (or
  `/rui topbar off`) takes the bar away, clock and slots too; the micro
  buttons then stand on the minimap block's wall, the lower row half over
  it, between the left end cap and the addon compartment's button (in two
  or three rows where one would make them too small), the time capsule
  sits on top of them (move it in Edit Mode, or Shift-drag it out of
  combat; `/rui clock reset` puts it back), and the buffs move up to the
  screen's top edge.

The three action slots beside the minimap are Reforged UI's own bar, so
all of Blizzard's action bars stay yours. Bind them under Key Bindings >
AddOns > Reforged UI. They need action slots of their own: they use the
moonkin form page (slots 109-111), which only druids use, and on druids the
shaman totem page (133-135). Drag spells, items and macros onto them out of
combat (with locked bars, hold Shift as usual). Up to 1.11 the slots were
Action Bar 8's first three buttons: on each character's first login with the
new version, what was on them and their keys move over, and Action Bar 8
goes back to off (the addon had turned it on).

Buffs and debuffs are held in the top-right corner just below the top bar
(at the screen's top edge with the top bar hidden).
Other frames that Edit Mode manages (cast bar, focus and party
frames, quest tracker) stay wherever Edit Mode puts them: place them around
the console there. Moving them from addon code breaks Blizzard's own code on
this client. (The stance bar's own frame stays put too, empty and
click-through; only its buttons move into the console.) The pet bar is placed
through the layout instead, see below.

**Edit Mode layout.** The first time each character logs in, the addon
switches it to an account-wide Edit Mode layout called "Reforged UI", made
once as a copy of the layout you were using, with the cast bar just above the
console (its default place is under it), raid-style party frames, and the
target frame placed for its aura icons (again at each login and target mode
change; the game only takes that in at a reload, so a mode change asks for
one, and a few seconds after login the chat says so if the icons aren't where
they belong, e.g. with another layout active). When the
layout is made, the raid frame options are turned on too: class colours,
power bars for every role, debuffs, aggro highlight, incoming heals, main
tank and assist, health as a percentage. Everything lives in the layout and
the game's options, so you can change any of it, or pick another layout, in
Edit Mode (on another layout the target frame and the rest stay where that
layout has them; chat says so after login and when Edit Mode closes). In
your other layouts a cast bar still in its default place is
moved above the console too. In every layout the pet bar, while still in its
default place (over the console), starts just above the stance row on the
console wall; once you move it in Edit Mode it stays where you put it.
After any such change the addon offers a reload: Blizzard applies layout
changes made by an addon as addon code, and its party frames would otherwise
error later (for example when Edit Mode closes).

**Damage meter.** The game's own damage meter is dressed in the theme by a
second addon, *Reforged UI: Damage Meter* (`ReforgedUI_DamageMeter`), which
ships with Reforged UI and shows as its own entry in the addon list, so it can
be left unloaded. Each meter window and its breakdown get the theme's top bar
trim around them (beam and posts, mitred at the corners), a dark inset, the theme's rail
under the header and every bar, and Warcraft III's bar texture and font. It only changes
art: the meter's numbers, its settings and its place (Edit Mode) are left to
Blizzard.

**Tooltips.** Reforged UI itself (`Tooltip.lua`) puts the same trim and inset
around the game's tooltips (the main one, clicked item links and the
comparison tooltips), with a unit's health bar inside the frame. Blizzard's
border is only made invisible, so "Themed tooltips" in the options or
`/rui tooltips off` brings it straight back.

**Bags.** A third addon, *Reforged UI: Bags* (`ReforgedUI_Bags`), dresses the
game's bag windows (each bag on its own, the combined backpack and the key
ring) the same way: the theme's trim around each window, a dark inset, the
theme's rail under the title and the bag's icon in Warcraft III's steel
button frame on the top-left corner, where Blizzard's round portrait was (its
menu still opens there). The items, money, search box and sorting are
Blizzard's. If you use **BetterBags**, the addon also adds a **Reforged UI**
theme to BetterBags' theme list (bag, bank and option windows, following
your Reforged UI theme as it changes); pick it in BetterBags' settings.
It is a theme for BetterBags' Sonata theme engine (BetterBags 0.5.17 and
later); with an older BetterBags, or none, that part does nothing. Using
**BetterBags Next** (BetterBags' new full-height bags)? It has its own theme
list, and **Reforged UI** is in that one too: the bags in your theme's dark
inset, a post of its trim down the side facing the middle of the screen (the
whole trim round a small bag), gold titles, and the race's own particles
drifting off the bags (the Light's stars, orc embers, night elf wisps, forge
sparks...).

**Spoken.** A fourth addon, *Reforged UI: Spoken* (`ReforgedUI_Spoken`), adds
a **Reforged UI** narrator style to [Spoken](https://github.com/rusty-key/spoken-wow),
the addon that reads quests, gossip, places and books aloud. It goes through
Spoken's public API (`Spoken:RegisterNarrator`): Spoken lists it among its
narrator styles (and offers it once, the first time both addons are
installed), and while it is the style, the narrator window is ours: the
theme's trim around it, a dark inset, the speaker's name in the theme's title
colour over its rail, then Spoken's own captions, a reading-position bar in
the theme's accent colour and Spoken's round controls. Spoken's settings page
gets a Reforged UI section while the style is chosen: **Frame follows the
speaker's race** (an orc's line in the Orc theme, a night elf's in the Night
Elf theme, whatever theme the UI wears), the window's size and locking it in
place (drag it anywhere otherwise). Without Spoken the addon does nothing.

## Options

The options live in the game's own options, under **Options > AddOns >
Reforged UI**, laid out like the game's: the cogwheel in the bottom-right
corner of the chat area (or `/rui config`) opens them ("Hide options
cogwheel" or `/rui cog off` takes the cogwheel away and gives its room to
the chat input box). The main page holds the theme, UI size, UI scale
(240-270), console transparency, themed tooltips and hiding the cogwheel
(and a Reload UI button); a page per part of the UI holds the rest:

- **Hero screen**: health and power as percentages, the low health
  threshold, the portrait (stop its animation, position and zoom), the four
  stat icons of this class and the reputation bar.
- **Target**: where the target shows (hero screen or wall plate), target
  aura size, target buffs first, your threat on the target, the wall plate
  (size, mirrored, back on the wall) and the movable target and target of
  target bars with their size.
- **Action bars**: hiding the grid texture, letting Edit Mode place bars
  1-3, and hiding the stance buttons or leaving them to a bar addon.
- **Chat**: chat width and height, the input box above the chat, moving and
  resizing the chat window yourself, and hiding the chat icons.
- **Top bar and minimap**: hiding the top bar, the time under the clock
  (server, local or hidden, 24 or 12 hour) and the zone text position.

Each page's **Defaults** button puts its options back. They are the original
addon's options, minus the layout ones (the centre modes, chat area width,
chat placement and hiding the bags: the console is always centred with its
chat area and inventory). (The micro buttons live in the top bar, or above
the minimap without it.)

**Let Edit Mode place action bars 1-3** (off by default) leaves bars 1-3 on
their own Edit Mode bars instead of in the grid: they are placed once over
the grid rows in the "Reforged UI" layout, at about the grid's icon size, and
from then on you can move, resize and reflow them (more rows, fewer icons) in
Edit Mode like any bar. The grid art is hidden while it is on.

**Let me move and resize the chat window** (off by default) puts the chat
window in the chat area once and then leaves it alone: unlock it from its
tab's menu (or use Edit Mode) to drag it anywhere and resize it. Its input box
follows it. Turning the option off puts it back in the chat area.

**Console transparency** (0% by default) makes the console's art
see-through, so the world shows through it: around 5-10% leaves silhouettes
visible without losing the look. Only the art fades; action buttons, icons,
the portrait, the minimap and the chat stay fully opaque. It is saved for the
whole account.

**UI size** (100% by default, down to 70%) makes the console and the top bar
smaller. The console stays on the bottom edge and spans the screen's width,
so on a smaller setting it simply takes up less of the screen's height. Edit
Mode's places for the target's auras and the cast bar follow when the slider
is let go. `/rui size 85` does the same. It is saved for the whole account.

The race themes keep their base faction's shapes and layout; only the colours
change. `tools/make_race_themes.py` makes them (see Development).

**Default theme.** `auto` (the default) picks the theme of your character's
race (`UnitRace("player")`): Human, Dwarf, Gnome, Night Elf, Orc, Tauren,
Troll and Undead (`Scourge`) each get their own; Undead characters get
Forsaken, and can pick the Scourge console instead. Skyborne is token `Skyborne`
with race id 95 ("High Order Skyborne") or 96 ("Windshaper Skyborne"); the id
picks the High Order or Windshapers theme. Without an id, the race name
("High Order", "Windshaper") or else the faction picks the variant.
Any other race gets its faction's default (Alliance: Human, Horde: Orc), and
later-expansion races take the closest theme (e.g. Dark Iron Dwarf: Dwarf).
Choosing a theme in the options or with `/rui theme` saves it and overrides the
race default until you pick `auto` again; `skyborne` picks the Skyborne theme
of your faction. Saved themes from earlier versions keep working.

## Setting up

1. Copy the `ReforgedUI` folder (and `ReforgedUI_DamageMeter`,
   `ReforgedUI_Bags` and `ReforgedUI_Spoken`, for the damage meter, bags and
   Spoken skins) into the AddOns
   folder of your Forever install.
   **Restart the game client completely** (not just `/reload`): the addon has
   new files, which the game only picks up on a full restart.
2. Action Bars 2 and 3 are turned on for you the first time each character
   logs in.
3. Move the focus frame and anything else Edit Mode manages to
   where you want them around the console.

## Commands

```
/rui config                      open the options (Options > AddOns > Reforged UI)
/rui cog on|off                   show or hide the options cogwheel in the chat area
/rui theme auto|human|dwarf|gnome|nightelf|highorder|orc|tauren|troll|forsaken|undead|windshapers|skyborne
/rui feeds                       list data feeds, game panels and top bar slots
/rui slot <number> <feed>|none   put a feed or game panel ("quests", "map") in a top bar slot
/rui size 70-100                 console and top bar size, in %
/rui scale 0.5-1.5               top bar scale
/rui layout auto|16:9|21:9|32:9  top bar layout
/rui topbar on|off               show or hide the top bar (menu buttons above the minimap when hidden)
/rui clock reset                 put the time back above the minimap (top bar hidden)
/rui target swap|plate           target display: on the hero screen, or a plate on the wall
/rui plate reset                 put the wall plate back on the wall (Shift-drag or Edit Mode moves it)
/rui plate size 50-150           the wall plate's size, in %
/rui plate mirror on|off         turn the wall plate round, portrait on the right
/rui repbar on|off               the reputation bar under the experience bar
/rui tooltips on|off             tooltips in the theme's frame, like the damage meter
/rui targetbar on|off|reset      a movable target health and power bar (Shift-drag it, or use Edit Mode)
/rui totbar on|off|reset         the same for the target's target
/rui barsize 100-200             both bars' size, in %
/rui aurasize 100-200            target buff and debuff icon size on the wall, in %
/rui auras reset                 target buffs and debuffs back on the wall after moving them in Edit Mode
/rui buffsfirst on|off           target buffs on the bottom rows, debuffs after them
/rui threat on|off               your threat % on the target, over its portrait and on the target bar
/rui module <console|hero|actionbars|minimap|chat|inventory|blizzard|target|topbar|config> on|off   (then /reload)
/rui status
/rui reset
```

## Not ported

Things the original addon does that have no taint-safe equivalent on this client, or that
the client now does itself:

- The **Customize** tab (moving and resizing every piece) and the eight
  custom themes.
- **Cast bar alignment**, the **buff position** option (buffs always sit under
  the top bar) and moving the **pet
  frame**: these are Edit Mode frames; place them in Edit Mode. (The stance
  buttons and the pet bar are placed, see above; the position options are not.)
- Moving Blizzard's **player status icons** (rest, combat, leader, master
  looter, PvP): replaced by our own icons in the same places (no master
  looter icon).
- The **"Center UI, no chat area"** modes, the **chat width** and **"Hide
  bags"** options: the console is always centred with its chat area and
  inventory, and the bags always show.
- **Horizontal multibars** (and their beta option), the **"Server is V+"**
  option and the **first-run reload** prompt.
- Spell and healing power **scanned from tooltips and auras**: the client's
  own spell power API is used instead.
- **Bonus action bar** handling (stances, stealth): the client pages the main
  bar by itself.
- Moving the **battleground minimap button**: it lines up with the other
  minimap buttons.
- The **chat scroll arrows** option hides the chat buttons beside the window
  instead (the client has no scroll arrows).
- Blizzard's player and target frames (and their pet and target of target
  frames) are hidden: the portrait block, our target display and our pet
  icon (Pet.lua, Shift-drag to move, `/rui pet reset`) replace them. The focus
  frame is left to Edit Mode.

## Art and licences

`ReforgedUI/art` is the original addon's art and font (the race theme folders are
recoloured copies of it) (`blq55.TTF`), cut from Warcraft III; the one `.dds` was converted to `.tga`. The top bar's
textures in `ReforgedUI/Media` are cropped from Warcraft III: Reforged (see
[Media/README.md](https://github.com/AlexHaible/WoW-UI-Addon/blob/master/ReforgedUI/Media/README.md)). Blizzard owns that art, and
the console art ships without a licence file, so keep this repository private.

`ReforgedUI/Libs` embeds LibStub (public domain), CallbackHandler-1.0 (BSD) and
LibDataBroker-1.1 (public domain) for the top bar's data feeds.

## Development

- `luacheck ReforgedUI` lints the addon.
- `lua5.1 tools/smoke_test.lua` loads the addon against a stubbed game API and
  exercises login, every theme, UI scale and screen shape, the
  hero screen, combat queuing and the main events.
- `python3 tools/make_race_themes.py [race ...]` regenerates the race themes'
  art (`ReforgedUI/art/<race>` and `ReforgedUI/Media/<Race>`) from the
  the original faction art: a gradient map per material (stone, trim, accents,
  dark fills) that keeps alpha and the original's shading. Palettes are at the
  top of the script. Needs Pillow and NumPy.
- `python3 tools/make_endcaps.py [theme ...]` builds the stand-in end caps
  (`art/<theme>/endcaps/endcap_{left,right}_gen.tga`) from each theme's
  inventory pillar. Real end cap art goes in as `endcap_left.tga` /
  `endcap_right.tga` and is listed in `Layout.ENDCAP_ART` with its size and
  overlap; it then replaces the stand-ins. Dwarf (hand-built art) borrows
  Human's until its own exist.
- `python3 tools/render_preview.py` re-renders the previews in `docs/previews`
  (`tools/dump_layout.lua` prints the layout as JSON).
- `Trim.lua` is the theme frame the damage meter, tooltip and bags skins put around
  Blizzard's windows (`ReforgedUI.CreateTrim`). `python3 tools/make_trim.py
  [theme ...]` makes its own art (`Media/Trim/`): the rail from each
  theme's target plate, the mitred corner where the top bar's beam and post
  meet, and side posts for themes whose top bar has none (Skyborne). The
  border itself is the top bar's trim from `Media/`. `python3
  tools/make_bb_frame.py` turns those pieces into the BetterBags theme's art
  (`frame.tga` for the classic bags, `beam.tga` and `post.tga` for
  BetterBags Next). `python3 tools/make_next_pillar.py` makes the leafier
  post (and swaying leaf clusters) Night Elf's full BetterBags Next panels
  stand against.
  `python3 tools/render_damage_meter.py out.png`,
  `python3 tools/render_bags.py out.png` and
  `python3 tools/render_spoken.py out.png` mock the skins up for every
  theme.
- `Layout.lua` holds all of the original addon's placement math, free of game API calls.

## [1.16.0](https://github.com/AlexHaible/WoW-UI-Addon/tree/1.16.0) (2026-11-20)

- Move the options into the game's options, on a page per part of the UI (#77)  
    The options menu becomes Options > AddOns > Reforged UI, drawn by the game's own settings panel: a main page (theme, UI size, UI scale, transparency, themed tooltips, hide the cogwheel, Reload UI) and pages for the hero screen, the target (including threat and the wall plate), action bars, chat, and the top bar and minimap, each in sections under headers with the game's Defaults button.  
    Every option is one row of Config.PAGES, a proxy setting over db.consoleOpts. Number boxes became sliders; theme, target display, time, clock, zone text and the stat icons are dropdowns. The cogwheel and /rui config open the page through Settings.OpenToCategory, which the game opens itself, so the panel manager stays untainted. Edit Mode placement after the size sliders waits until a slider settles.  
- Add an option to hide the options cogwheel (#76)  
    "Hide options cogwheel" in the menu (consoleOpts.hideCog, /rui cog on|off)  
    takes the cogwheel out of the chat area and lets the chat input box run the  
    full width. The menu still opens with /rui config or Options > AddOns.  
- Show your threat % on the target (#75)  
    Your threat on the target (as in its tooltip) shows over its portrait and on the target bar, coloured by threat status, while you are on its threat list. Option "Show threat on target" and /rui threat on|off.  
- Let players move, resize and mirror the wall plate (#74)  
    The wall plate gets its own frame, placed from the screen's bottom centre  
    (consoleOpts.targetPlateSpot), sized 50-150 % (targetPlateSize) and  
    optionally turned round (targetPlateMirror). Shift-drag out of combat or  
    drag in Edit Mode (where it shows as a stand-in without a target). Its  
    cast bar, combo points, level plate and tag are placed on it; the secure  
    target button and the target of target follow out of combat; the target  
    frame's aura spot follows through the Edit Mode layout (after Edit Mode  
    closes when moved there). /rui plate reset|size|mirror, options slider,  
    checkbox and reset button, smoke tests, README and CurseForge text.

## [1.15.0](https://github.com/AlexHaible/WoW-UI-Addon/tree/1.15.0) (2026-11-13)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/AlexHaible/WoW-UI-Addon/compare/1.14.3...1.15.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/AlexHaible/WoW-UI-Addon/releases)

- Move a druid's minimap slots off the shaman totem slots (#73)  
    Druids' minimap slots were 133-135, the shaman totem bar's slots, which only take Fire, Earth and Water totem spells. Druids now use page 11 (121-123). The hearthstone is retried once for druids and only counted as placed once it is there; an action a slot refuses goes back to its old slot.  
- Mark rare, elite and boss targets on every target display (#72)  
    A tag over the portrait (swap and wall plate) and on the target bars' top edge says Rare, Elite, Rare Elite or Boss in the colours of Blizzard's dragons; the word in the level line and the mark after the bars' level are coloured the same way.  
- Share how our movable frames are dragged, and one Edit Mode hook (#71)  
    Core.lua has ns:MakeDraggable, ns:StartDrag, ns:StopDrag and ns:OnEditMode, used by the target bars, the pet's icon, the totem and stance rows and the time capsule. The smoke test checks them and fails if another file moves a frame or hooks Edit Mode itself.  
- List every option with its default, and test that no other is used (#70)  
    clockTime and clockHours get the defaults the code fell back to, the options that stay unset until used are listed as such, and the smoke test fails when the addon reads or sets an option Core.lua doesn't list.  
- Read secret values through one set of helpers (#69)  
    Core.lua has ns.IsSecret, ns.IsKnown and ns.IsNumber, and every file uses those instead of asking the game itself. The smoke test fails on another file calling issecretvalue and ends with an in-an-instance pass.  
- Give Edit Mode its own file, and list the frames placed in every layout under one rule (#68)  
    The Edit Mode code moves from Core.lua into EditMode.lua. The cast bar, buffs, pet bar and leave vehicle button are entries of one list sharing one placing rule; the smoke test checks that each has a name and saved spot of its own and that a relog saves nothing.  
- Hand out the options menu's rows, and test that no two options overlap (#67)  
    Options take the next row of their column or of the list at the bottom instead of a hand-picked position, the menu's height follows its last row, and the smoke test fails when two options overlap or one leaves the menu. Every option stays where it was.  
- Add a movable target of target bar and a size for both bars (#66)  
    A player asked to move the target and target of target windows (e.g. to the right, over the bags) and for the target of target to look like the target window. The target of target bar is the same window as the target bar for the target's target (consoleOpts.totBar / totBarPos, /rui totbar). Both bars get a shared size, 100-200 % (Target bar size slider, /rui barsize), and stand in HIGH strata so they can sit over the console's buttons.  
- Let players hide the stance buttons (#65)  
    Hide stance buttons option (/rui stance hide|show): invisible and click-through, key bindings still work.  
- Take the target buffs along when the target display switches, and say when another Edit Mode layout is active (#64)  
    Since 1.13.2 a Target Frame anywhere but our last places counted as moved by the player and stayed put, even across a switch from swap to the wall plate. Edit Mode re-anchors a frame that is only clicked (another anchor point, snapped), which our offset comparison took for a move. Now a frame within a few units of our places (wherever its anchor point) is still ours, and a target display switch always puts the frame in the new display's place.  
    On any Edit Mode layout other than "Reforged UI", chat now says so a few seconds after login and when Edit Mode closes, once per layout and session: the target's buffs and debuffs aren't placed there, and other frames only leave their default place.
